title: Rank-one enlargement of the open cell
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $P=(G,T=D_A(M),\Phi,\Phi^\vee,\Delta,(X_\alpha))$ a pinned split realization [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Use the root subgroups, Weyl elements $n_\alpha$, ordered root-product subgroups $U_\Psi$ and open cell $\Omega=U^-TU^+$ of [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], with $U^\pm=U_{\pm\Phi^+}$. For a simple root $\alpha$ put $L_\alpha=M\cap\mathbf Q\alpha$, $S_\alpha=D_A(M/L_\alpha)\subseteq T$, and let $K_\alpha=Z_G(S_\alpha)$ be the centralizer functor whose points commute with $S_\alpha$ after every further algebra extension. Set $V_\alpha^+=U_{\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha\}}$ and $V_\alpha^-=U_{(-\Phi^+)\setminus\{-\alpha\}}$. These root sets are closed in the sense of the root-calculus node. The functor $K_\alpha$ is represented by a smooth affine reductive closed subgroup of $G$, contains $T,U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ and $n_\alpha$, and has precisely the roots $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ relative to $T$. Multiplication gives an open immersion
$$j_\alpha:V_\alpha^-\times_A K_\alpha\times_A V_\alpha^+\longrightarrow G.$$
Writing $J_\alpha$ for its image, one has the equality of open subschemes
$$\Omega=j_\alpha\bigl(V_\alpha^-\times_A(U_{-\alpha}TU_\alpha)\times_A V_\alpha^+\bigr).$$
Here $U_{-\alpha}\times_A T\times_A U_\alpha\to K_\alpha$ is itself an open immersion with the indicated image. All inclusions and open immersions commute with arbitrary base change. Empty $V_\alpha^\pm$ products mean the identity subgroup; if $\Delta$ is empty the assertions indexed by $\alpha$ are vacuous.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.7(4), printed p.113, and Theorem 5.1.13, printed pp.143--145: choose a cocharacter zero on the simple root and positive on the other simple roots; its centralizer is the rank-one Levi factor. This is geometry of the enlarged cell, with no target group or homomorphism data. Read online; archival literature copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this root-group geometric assertion.

proof.text: Write $\alpha=d\alpha_0$ with $d>0$ and $\alpha_0$ primitive in $M$. In coordinates on a basis of $M$, dividing the coordinates of $\alpha$ by their greatest common divisor and using Bezout gives $L_\alpha=\mathbf Z\alpha_0$. The group algebra quotient by $e_{\alpha_0}-1$ is $A[M/\mathbf Z\alpha_0]$, so $S_\alpha=\ker\chi_{\alpha_0}$ as subgroup functors, exactly the torus of the rank-one-centralizer theorem. Apply that theorem (after choosing a basis of $M$) to obtain a smooth affine finitely presented reductive closed subgroup $K_\alpha$ with connected geometric fibres and Lie module $\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\mathfrak g_\alpha\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$, with precisely the roots $\pm\alpha$. The torus $T$ centralizes $S_\alpha$. Since $\pm\alpha$ restrict trivially to $S_\alpha$, the root-conjugation formula shows on every test algebra and every further extension that $U_{\pm\alpha}\subseteq K_\alpha$. The displayed word defining $n_\alpha$ then puts $n_\alpha$ in $K_\alpha(A)$.

Extend the linearly independent set $\Delta$ to a rational basis of $M\otimes\mathbf Q$. Give $\alpha$ value zero, the other simple roots value one, and the supplementary basis vectors value zero. Clearing a positive common denominator on a lattice basis gives $\lambda\in M^\vee$ with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle=0$ and $\langle\beta,\lambda\rangle>0$ for $\beta\in\Delta\setminus\{\alpha\}$. Every positive root other than $\alpha$ has a positive coefficient at another simple root: otherwise reducedness makes it $\alpha$. Thus the roots of positive, zero and negative $\lambda$-weight are respectively $\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha\}$, $\{\pm\alpha\}$ and $(-\Phi^+)\setminus\{-\alpha\}$. A nonempty sum of roots from the first set retains positive weight and nonnegative simple-root coefficients, so if it is a root it stays in that set; likewise for the last set. This proves the required closedness. Both sets are disjoint from their negatives.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, printed pp.143-144, choice of an integral cocharacter; here choose the face corresponding to the simple root.

proof.text: Use conjugation by the monomial cocharacter $\lambda$ as the action $a$ in the dynamic-subgroup theorem. Write its subgroups as $Z_\lambda,U_\lambda,P_\lambda,U_{-\lambda}$. They are smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroups with connected geometric fibres. Their Lie modules, from the theorem and the weight computation in step 2, are $\operatorname{Lie}(Z_\lambda)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\mathfrak g_\alpha\oplus\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(U_{\pm\lambda})=\bigoplus_{\gamma\in\pm\Phi^+\setminus\{\pm\alpha\}}\mathfrak g_\gamma$. Since $\lambda(\alpha_0)=0$, the cocharacter factors through $S_\alpha$, giving $K_\alpha\subseteq Z_\lambda$. For $\gamma$ of positive weight, the formula $\lambda(t)\exp_\gamma(v)\lambda(t)^{-1}=\exp_\gamma(t^{\langle\gamma,\lambda\rangle}v)$ extends over $t=0$ with value $1$; hence $U_\gamma\subseteq U_\lambda$ on all test algebras. The negative-weight case uses $-\lambda$. Ordered multiplication from the root-calculus theorem now gives closed subgroup inclusions $V_\alpha^\pm\subseteq U_{\pm\lambda}$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.7(1)-(4), printed pp.112-114; Theorem 5.1.13 proof, pp.143-144.

proof.text: Check these three inclusions on a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field. For $K_\alpha\subseteq Z_\lambda$, take the smooth connected closed subgroups $T,U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ of $Z_\lambda$; for $V_\alpha^\pm\subseteq U_{\pm\lambda}$ take its root subgroups. The field root-parametrization theorem ensures each root subgroup is smooth, connected, closed and has tangent space $\mathfrak g_\gamma$; the torus has the analogous properties. In each case their tangent spaces span the target tangent space by step 3. Apply the smooth-subgroup tangent-generation theorem, with its closed subgroup denoted there by $K$ equal to our $K_\alpha$ or $V_\alpha^\pm$, to conclude equality as subgroup schemes on that fibre. The targets are smooth connected affine finite-type groups by the dynamic theorem, so all hypotheses are met, including an empty root family. The three inclusions are locally finitely presented: their affine source and target algebras are finitely presented over $A$, and a finite relative presentation is obtained by adjoining source generators and adding the finitely many equations identifying target generators with their images. Their sources are smooth over $A$ by the centralizer and root-calculus theorems. The geometric-fibre isomorphism criterion therefore gives $K_\alpha=Z_\lambda$ and $V_\alpha^\pm=U_{\pm\lambda}$ over $A$.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.13 proof, printed pp.143-144, equality of smooth closed subgroups via Lie algebras and geometric-fibre isomorphism test; the general tangent-generation input is Milne Corollary 10.17, printed p.191; geometric-fibre test: Stacks Tag 039E, lemma-morphism-between-flat.

proof.text: The dynamic theorem identifies $Z_\lambda\times_A U_\lambda$ with $P_\lambda$ by $(z,u)\mapsto zu$ and makes $U_{-\lambda}\times_A P_\lambda\to G$ an open immersion. Substitute the three subgroup equalities of step 4. The resulting composite is exactly $(v_-,k,v_+)\mapsto v_-kv_+$, so it is the required open immersion $j_\alpha$. Denote its open image by $J_\alpha$.

The pair $(K_\alpha,T)$ with roots $\{\pm\alpha\}$, inherited coroots and pinning generator $X_\alpha$ is a pinned split realization: the centralizer theorem gives the root modules and reductivity, $T$ is fibrewise maximal since it was maximal in $G$, and the root-calculus theorem identifies its root exponentials and coroots with those of $G$. Apply its open-cell assertion to this rank-one realization. It gives an open immersion $U_{-\alpha}\times_A T\times_A U_\alpha\to K_\alpha$ with image $\Omega_\alpha=U_{-\alpha}TU_\alpha$. In the ordered product coordinates of $G$, enumerate the negative roots with $-\alpha$ last and the positive roots with $\alpha$ first. The root-calculus theorem then gives product isomorphisms $V_\alpha^-\times_A U_{-\alpha}\simeq U^-$ and $U_\alpha\times_A V_\alpha^+\simeq U^+$. Associativity identifies the restriction of $j_\alpha$ to $V_\alpha^-\times_A\Omega_\alpha\times_A V_\alpha^+$, in these product coordinates, with the open-cell map $U^-\times_A T\times_A U^+\to G$. Thus its image equals $\Omega$ as an open subscheme, not merely on geometric points.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4, printed p.110, and Theorem 5.1.13, printed pp.143-145, arbitrary ordering and open cell.

proof.text: The rank-one centralizer and all its inclusions commute with arbitrary base change by the centralizer theorem, and root exponentials and ordered root products do so by the root-calculus theorem. The dynamic theorem gives the same property for its subgroups and maps. All maps just constructed are multiplication restrictions, so their base changes are the same restrictions for the base-changed objects. Open immersions remain open immersions after base change; their open images are the inverse-image open subschemes. Consequently $j_\alpha$, its rank-one restriction, and the equality of open subschemes in step 6 commute with arbitrary base change. The zero target ring gives empty schemes and the same assertion trivially. If the complementary root sets are empty their products are the identity subgroup, as in the root-calculus statement; when $\Delta$ is empty no $\alpha$ is selected and all assertions are vacuous.
